_readme: MCP servers Kryptonite may start. Same shape as Claude Desktop and Claude Code,
so a server block can be copied between them verbatim.
LOCAL (stdio) - the server runs as a child process on this machine:
command   executable. On Windows, npx/npm/uvx shims are handled for you.
args      argument list.
env       merged over the extension host's environment.
cwd       defaults to the workspace root.
REMOTE - the server is reached over the network:
url       https://... A plain http:// url to anywhere but localhost is
refused, because the headers below would travel in clear text.
headers   sent on every request, which is where a token belongs.
type      omit for Streamable HTTP, which is what current servers speak.
'sse' selects the older HTTP+SSE protocol - a different wire,
not a variation, so only set it if the server documents it.
BOTH:
approval  'ask' (default) routes every call through the approval gate;
'auto' does not. A server is someone else's code.
timeoutMs per-request budget. The first start of an npx-launched server
includes a package download; the handshake allows 45s minimum.
enabled   false keeps the block here without starting anything.
${VAR} and ${VAR:-default} expand from the environment in command, args,
env, cwd, url and headers - so a token never has to be written into this
file, which lives in the workspace and usually gets committed.
Tools reach the model as mcp__<server>__<tool>. They are withheld entirely in
Ask and Plan mode - neither promises the model can only look, and MCP has
no way to declare a tool read-only, so there is nothing to check.
filesystem and memory below are live, and both are verified for real by
test/mcp-live.ts - not parsed, actually spawned, and actually called.
deepwiki is this repo's own server (see below); it is exercised by its own
Python test suite under mcp-servers/tests rather than by mcp-live.ts.
filesystem exposes read/write tools scoped to the directory named in args -
the workspace root here, and nothing above it. approval is 'ask', so every
call still stops for you first.
memory is a second shape on purpose: a local knowledge graph rather than
another filesystem reader, so it demonstrates a stateful tool - create an
entity, search for it later. It keeps its graph in its own process, next to
the installed package, not inside this workspace; set the MEMORY_FILE_PATH
env var here if you want it to persist somewhere specific instead.
deepwiki is one of THIS repo's own servers (mcp-servers/), and the odd one
out: it does not reach an external system, it reads this workspace and
generates a wiki of it through a Genesis endpoint - then serves that wiki
back so any agent can understand the codebase before editing it. It runs
straight from the checkout via 'python -m deepwiki_mcp.server' with
PYTHONPATH set to mcp-servers/src (cwd is the workspace root, so the
relative path resolves and DEEPWIKI_WORKSPACE defaults to this repo). After
'pip install ./mcp-servers' the console script 'deepwiki-mcp' is the
equivalent command. Its READ tools - wiki_status, list_wiki_pages,
read_wiki_page, search_wiki - need no endpoint and work offline; only
generate_wiki and ask_wiki reach the model, and they name the missing
DEEPWIKI_ENDPOINT_URL/_MODEL at call time rather than blocking startup. Set
those two (and DEEPWIKI_ENDPOINT_KEY unless the endpoint needs none) in your
environment - the ${VAR:-} passthroughs below keep them out of this file.
